facts.statement: Cyrilavis lived in the Early Eocene of the United States within the Fossil Butte Member of the Green River Formation.
facts.quote: Cyrilavis is an extinct genus of halcyornithid bird from the Early Eocene Fossil Butte Member of the Green River Formation, United States.

facts.statement: A complete skeleton from the Green River Formation was originally described in 1976 as the species Primobucco olsoni.
facts.quote: A complete skeleton of a bird from the Green River Formation was described as "Primobucco" olsoni in 1976 from the specimens GSATC 217 as a relative to the Bucconidae based on its zygodactyl foot configuration.

facts.statement: The genus name Cyrilavis was established in 2010 to replace Primobucco because the bird was reclassified as a halcyornithid rather than a puffbird relative.
facts.quote: In 2010 the genus Cyrilavis was erected to accomdoate the halcyornithid, since it was no longer thought to be closely related to the Bucconidae, with the new name Cyrilavis olsoni.

facts.statement: The genus name Cyrilavis honors the paleontologist Cyril Walker.
facts.quote: The generic name Cyrilavis is in honour of Cyril Walker, a notable paleontologist of early Cenozoic birds.

facts.statement: A second species, Cyrilavis colburnorum, was described in 2011 based on a nearly complete skeleton.
facts.quote: In 2011, Ksepka et al. described a new species, Cyrilavis colburnorum, with the holotype FMNH PA 754, a nearly complete skeleton.

facts.statement: Cyrilavis possessed a relatively large head.
facts.quote: Cyrilavis was a relatively large-headed bird.

facts.statement: The beak of Cyrilavis was approximately half the length of the head and expanded from top to bottom.
facts.quote: The beak is about half of the total length of the head, and is dorsoventrally expanded.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence from C. olsoni indicates a feathered halo around the head interpreted as a crest.
facts.quote: Cyrilavis olsoni, whose holotype preserves feathering, shows a halo of feathers around the head, interpreted as a crest.

facts.statement: In Cyrilavis, the hand bone (manus) is much shorter than the forearm bone (ulna), which contrasts with the anatomy of modern parrots.
facts.quote: As in all other halcyornithids and in the psittacopasseran Psittacopes, the manus is much shorter than the ulna. This is the opposite of the condition found in extant parrots.

facts.statement: Cyrilavis belongs to the Halcyornithidae, a group that split before parrots and songbirds diverged, making it equally related to both.
facts.quote: Recent analyses have found that the Halcyornithidae, to which Cyrilavis belongs, diverged before the split between parrots and passerines, meaning it is equally closely related to both orders.

facts.statement: Cyrilavis lived between 56 and 48.07 million years ago during the Ypresian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Ypresian (56 to 48.07 million years ago)
